The Hornets, fresh from their FA Trophy triumph over Torquay United, travel to Kent to take on the Whites this Saturday.

And Dover are ‘having the season of all seasons’, according to Di Paola.

Did you know with an ad-lite subscription to SussexWorld, you get 70% fewer ads while viewing the news that matters to you.

The Whites will welcome former Premier League champions Leicester City to the Megger Community Stadium in the second round proper of the FA Cup on Saturday, December 5 after beating division-above Wealdstone in the previous round.

Dover, who boast former Hornet Jack Bates among their ranks, sit 13th in the National League South, level on 22 points with 12th-placed Horsham albeit with two games in hand.

Recent findings suggest that di Paola told us: “Dover are having the seasons of all seasons with the FA Cup run. Dover are in the play-off mix, they’ve got their FA Cup tie against Leicester, they’ve clearly got a good thing going on.

It has been revealed that “It’s always tough down there. They’ve got a major, wide pitch and big crowds usually and they’ve got some really good players down there, including Batesy [Bates] who was with us last year very briefly.

It has been revealed that “It’ll be a good test up there. As I mentioned, they’re in great form and they’re an athletic, mobile side. They’re a major, powerful team who put it on you and make you defend.

Recent findings suggest that “We’re going to have to be resolute and strong mentally and physically to cope with them. It’s going to be another tough challenge for our boys but hopefully we’ll be okay in terms of the squad.”.

The Hornets will then welcome Truro on Tuesday evening, with the visitors facing a round trip of around 505 miles for the midweek encounter at the Fusion Aviation Community Stadium.

The Tinners have impressed since dropping down into step two after relegation from the National League in 2025-26.

The Cornwall outfit are, at the time of writing, fourth in the table and unbeaten in seven in the league, winning four out of their last five.

And Di Paola has predicted another formidable challenge against ‘one of the favourites for the title’.

Recent findings suggest that he added: “I haven’t done anything on Truro yet. We’ll take a good look at that after Dover on Saturday.

In a recent development, “I think they are one of the favourites for the title so that’ll be a tough game. I’ve watched them seven or eight times when watching some of the teams we’ve played, and they’re a good side.”.

Horsham have no fresh injury concerns, with midfielder Ronan Silva closing in on a return to action.

Di Paola said: “Ronan is almost back. We could have put him on the bench on Saturday, so hopefully by the weekend he’ll be good to go back into the squad.”.

Coventry City vs. Crystal Palace: Head-to-head record and past meetings before Premier League clash

📅 19 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 4 min read (811 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Co

⏱️ ~4 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • By Seye Omidiora | 19 Nov 2026 22:55.
  • Coventry City welcome Crystal Palace to the Coventry Building Society Arena this weekend in a crucial Premier League relegation clash following the November international break.
  • Frank Lampard's 17th-placed Sky Blues sit just one point above the bottom three after a 3-1 defeat at Everton, though October home wins over Newcastle United and Sunderland offer encouragement as they chase consecutive top-flight victories on their own turf.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

By Seye Omidiora | 19 Nov 2026 22:55.

Coventry City welcome Crystal Palace to the Coventry Building Society Arena this weekend in a crucial Premier League relegation clash following the November international break.

Frank Lampard's 17th-placed Sky Blues sit just one point above the bottom three after a 3-1 defeat at Everton, though October home wins over Newcastle United and Sunderland offer encouragement as they chase consecutive top-flight victories on their own turf.

Meanwhile, upcoming Palace boss Thomas Frank takes charge for the first time with less than a week of training under his belt, tasked with ending a four-match losing run and lifting the London club above their West Midlands hosts.

Here, Sports Mole takes a closer look at the head-to-head record and past meetings between Coventry and Crystal Palace.

Over 118 years have passed since Coventry City and Crystal Palace first locked horns - an FA Cup tie in January 1908 that ended in a 4-2 victory for the Eagles - and there have now been 114 competitive meetings between the two clubs across all competitions.

There is very little to separate the sides historically, with the Sky Blues holding the narrowest of edges on 41 victories, while Palace are hot on their heels with 38 wins and another 35 encounters have ended all square.

More than 14 years have elapsed since their most recent clash in March 2012, when the two teams shared the spoils in a 1-1 Championship draw in the West Midlands several months after Palace had edged a 2-1 victory at Selhurst Park.

Coventry's last triumphs in this fixture came during the 2010-11 campaign, when they recorded back-to-back 2-1 home wins in the FA Cup and Championship in January and February 2011 to avenge a 2-0 defeat in South London earlier that season.

Prior to that double, Palace had enjoyed a dominant spell over the Sky Blues, putting together a 10-match unbeaten run across all competitions between September 2005 and November 2009 that included seven wins and three draws.

That sequence featured five consecutive victories for the Londoners - highlighted by emphatic 4-1 and 4-2 away triumphs - before Coventry finally ended their hoodoo with a gritty 1-0 win at Selhurst Park in February 2010.

This weekend's showdown marks their first Premier League meeting in over 28 years, with the clubs last crossing paths in the top flight in February 1998 when Coventry ran out 3-0 winners in South London.

Across their six previous Premier League encounters, the Sky Blues hold the upper hand with two victories to Palace's one alongside three draws, and remarkably neither side has ever won a home game in the competition.

Palace's lone Premier League success in this fixture was a 4-1 away demolition in November 1994, whereas Coventry claimed 2-0 and 3-0 victories on the road in February 1995 and February 1998 respectively.

Before the Premier League era, Coventry were a formidable force against Palace in the old First Division, going unbeaten in their first 14 top-flight meetings between 1969 and 1990 - winning 10 and drawing four - before the Eagles finally broke their duck with a 2-1 win in December 1990.

Knockout meetings have been rare, with Palace winning three of their four cup ties - including 3-0 and 1-0 League Cup successes in 2002 and 2005 - while Coventry's most emphatic results in the fixture date back to their Division Three (South) days in the 1930s, when they dished out 8-0 and 8-1 home thrashings in 1932 and 1935.

Mar 06, 2012: Coventry 1-1 Crystal Palace (Championship).

Aug 16, 2011: Crystal Palace 2-1 Coventry (Championship).

Feb 12, 2011: Coventry 2-1 Crystal Palace (Championship).

Jan 08, 2011: Coventry 2-1 Crystal Palace (FA Cup).

Nov 13, 2010: Crystal Palace 2-0 Coventry (Championship).

Feb 20, 2010: Crystal Palace 0-1 Coventry (Championship).

Nov 21, 2009: Coventry 1-1 Crystal Palace (Championship).

Apr 07, 2009: Crystal Palace 1-1 Coventry (Championship).

Nov 08, 2008: Coventry 0-2 Crystal Palace (Championship).

Dec 26, 2007: Coventry 0-2 Crystal Palace (Championship).

Sep 18, 2007: Crystal Palace 1-1 Coventry (Championship).

Jan 13, 2007: Coventry 2-4 Crystal Palace (Championship).

Nov 22, 2005: Crystal Palace 2-0 Coventry (Championship).

Oct 15, 2005: Coventry 1-4 Crystal Palace (Championship).

May 09, 2004: Coventry 2-1 Crystal Palace (League Division One).

The 67-year-old was appointed interim head coach after the sacking of Colin Kazim-Richards in October with the club bottom of League Two.

A club statement read: “Over the past few weeks, the club has been working hard to make the right appointment and has been carefully weighing up the options to ensure that the appointment is the right one for the team and the club as a whole.

“During this process, Kevin Blackwell made a strong impression on club leadership, making him a strong candidate for the role as the weeks progressed.

“Kevin’s leadership skills, work ethic and desire have made a strong impression on club staff and the first-team squad, and the club’s leadership team are committed to ensuring the positive mentality remains in the building as we approach a run of crucial games.

“Kevin has the full support of everyone at the football club, as we look to turn over a latest page on our season and climb back up the table.”.

According to recent reports, and Blackwell was pleased. He noted: “I'm delighted to stay here. I have to say, I've been so impressed with what I've seen around the place. As I've said before in my press conferences, Raph [Raphael Khalili] and the ownership have supported everything that I've asked them to do. We're bringing in new staff, the club's taken a whole new vamp.

It has been revealed that “I have to say, the thing that really persuaded me at the end was the players. I think their attitude has been absolutely fabulous. I can honestly tell you we've done some really hard sessions here, as hard as I've known.

“While they've found it tough, not one of them has complained about it and they've worked hard. I'm really here because the players have really helped make my mind up. I was, as you know, 50-50 what I was going to do, but let's say two weeks here, I've liked what I've seen.".

In the coming weeks, Kevin will be making further appointments to his coaching team, following the recent arrival of Jordan Tait.

A statement from ownership will follow shortly.
